definitions.explanation: Telling someone you have romantic feelings for them.
Openly admitting to something, especially a crime or wrongdoing.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}に{告白|こくはく}したが、{振|ふ}られた。
examples.english: I confessed my feelings to her, but was rejected.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{罪|つみ}を{告白|こくはく}した。
examples.english: The criminal confessed to the crime.

examples.japanese: {告白|こくはく}するタイミングを{待|ま}っている。
examples.english: I'm waiting for the right time to confess my feelings.

notes:
VERB FORM:
{告白|こくはく}する (to confess)

USAGE:
Sense 1 (love confession) is extremely common in Japanese culture:
・{告白|こくはく}する (to confess one's feelings)
・{告白|こくはく}される (to be confessed to)
・{告白|こくはく}を{受|う}ける (to receive a confession)

This is the typical way relationships begin in Japan, especially among young people. Popular settings include after school, during festivals, or before graduation.

Sense 2 (admission of guilt) is used in more formal contexts:
・{告白|こくはく}{記|き} - confession, memoir
・{罪|つみ}の{告白|こくはく} - confession of sin

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{自白|じはく} - confession (legal, to police)
・{白状|はくじょう} - confession, admission
・{懺悔|ざんげ} - confession (religious)
